repos.description: Docker container for managing Nginx proxy hosts with a simple, powerful interface

notes.audience: Các lập trình viên, homelabber và quản trị viên VPS/game-server tại Việt Nam muốn tối ưu hạ tầng mạng và gom toàn bộ reverse proxy, DDNS, NAT traversal và tunnel vào một công cụ duy nhất.
notes.angle: Thay vì dựng riêng Nginx Proxy Manager để reverse proxy và chạy script dựng FRP/Cloudflared phức tạp, Gately gom toàn bộ reverse proxy, WAF, STUN, DDNS và quản lý tunnel vào một binary Go gọn nhẹ quản lý trực quan trên cổng 16680.

facts.fact: Gately là gateway mạng mã nguồn mở (Apache-2.0) viết bằng Go, tích hợp DDNS, STUN NAT traversal, port forwarding, reverse proxy, chứng chỉ ACME, WAF, Tailscale, frp, Cloudflare Tunnel và web terminal trong một binary.
facts.quote: Open-source, auditable network gateway for homelabs, NAS and servers: DDNS, STUN traversal, port forwarding with SNI routing, reverse proxy and web server, ACME certificates, WAF, Tailscale, frp

facts.fact: Gately tích hợp tính năng Protocol Routing giúp tối đa 20 giao thức mạng (như HTTPS, SSH, RDP, OpenVPN) có thể chia sẻ chung một cổng duy nhất mà không cần giải mã lưu lượng.
facts.quote: Identifies the protocol from the first bytes of each connection so HTTPS, SSH, RDP, OpenVPN and 20 protocols in total share one port; TLS is routed by SNI and ALPN, HTTP by Host

facts.fact: Gately không đóng gói sẵn Tailscale, NetBird, frp hay cloudflared mà quản lý tiến trình ngoài, hỗ trợ tự tải phiên bản ổn định từ upstream, cài vào thư mục bin/ và lưu giữ 3 phiên bản cũ để rollback 1-click.
facts.quote: These four modules manage the official external programs (automatic restart, logs aggregated in the UI). Gately does not bundle them. The "online install" card on each module page downloads the latest

facts.fact: Gately lưu trữ token/key cấu hình với quyền 0600 và truyền token cloudflared qua biến môi trường để tránh bị lộ trong danh sách tiến trình hệ thống.
facts.quote: Tokens and keys in config files are stored with 0600 permissions, and the cloudflared token is passed via an environment variable so it never appears in the process list.

facts.fact: Tường lửa WAF của Gately được xây dựng dựa trên engine Coraza kết hợp bộ quy tắc OWASP CRS v4, có thể bật ở chế độ phát hiện (detection) hoặc chặn (blocking) riêng cho từng trang web.
facts.quote: Coraza + OWASP CRS v4, blocking or detection only

facts.fact: Gately hỗ trợ tính năng Network Topology vẽ trực tiếp luồng traffic từ visitor qua listener và site đến backend với 7 kiểu hiển thị và hỗ trợ ẩn IP/domain trước khi chia sẻ.
facts.quote: Seven layouts: tree, vertical, radial, Sankey, sunburst, treemap and bubbles

facts.fact: Dung lượng binary của Gately khoảng 32 MB, yêu cầu router OpenWrt phải có đủ dung lượng tương đương trên phân vùng /overlay, do đó không hỗ trợ các router flash 16 MB hoặc 32 MB.
facts.quote: The binary is about 32 MB and needs the same amount of free space (check with df -h /overlay), which suits x86 soft routers, ARM64 boxes and other devices with ample storage; routers with 16 MB / 32 MB of flash are too small

facts.fact: Khác với Nginx Proxy Manager đã dừng hỗ trợ kiến trúc armv7 từ bản v2.14+, Gately vẫn cung cấp bản build Docker và binary cho amd64, arm64 và arm/v7.
facts.quote: `armv7` is no longer supported in version 2.14+. This is due to Nodejs dropping support for armhf. Please use the `2.13.7` image tag if this applies to you.

facts.fact: Nginx Proxy Manager tập trung chuyên biệt vào việc proxy hosts và SSL termination trên nền Nginx với giao diện Tabler UI chạy ở cổng 81.
facts.quote: When your docker container is running, connect to it on port `81` for the admin interface.

facts.fact: Gately hỗ trợ reverse proxy domain với HTTPS và HTTP/3, áp dụng thay đổi cấu hình tức thời mà không làm gián đoạn hay ngắt các kết nối mạng hiện có.
facts.quote: Reverse proxy, static files and redirects by domain, with HTTPS and HTTP/3. Each site gets its own WAF, IP rules and sign-in, and changes apply without dropping connections.

facts.fact: Dự án cam kết dữ liệu và cấu hình lưu trữ cục bộ trên máy chủ của người dùng, mặc định không kết nối về máy chủ dự án và không thu thập bất kỳ báo cáo dữ liệu nào.
facts.quote: Open source under Apache-2.0; your config and data stay on your own device, and nothing is collected or reported.

caveats: Mật khẩu mặc định là gately.cn được công khai rộng rãi; giao diện sẽ liên tục hiện cảnh báo yêu cầu đổi mật khẩu ngay sau lần đầu đăng nhập.
Khuyến nghị chạy chế độ host network khiến Gately dùng chung dải cổng với host, dễ gây xung đột nếu host đã mở cổng 16680, 80 hoặc 443.
Các chương trình mạng phụ trợ (frpc/frps, tailscale, netbird, cloudflared, filebrowser) không có sẵn trong image/binary mà phải cài online từ giao diện hoặc tự chép binary vào thư mục bin/.
Tailscale chỉ cung cấp gói chạy sẵn trực tiếp cho hệ điều hành Linux; trên Windows/macOS người dùng phải cài app Tailscale chính thức rồi trỏ đường dẫn thủ công vào Gately.

Gói cài đặt trên router OpenWrt nặng khoảng 32 MB, không cài được trên các dòng router bộ nhớ flash nhỏ 16 MB hoặc 32 MB; kiến trúc ARM trên OpenWrt bắt buộc phải là ARMv7 có phần cứng floating point (FPU).
Bản cài đặt fnOS (.fpk) chạy trực tiếp dưới quyền root để mở port 80/443 và quản lý Docker, tài liệu khuyến cáo chỉ nên cài đặt trên NAS thuộc quyền kiểm soát an toàn.
Trên OpenWrt 25.12 trở lên dùng trình quản lý apk, gói cài đặt chưa được ký nên bắt buộc phải truyền thêm cờ --allow-untrusted khi cài.
gaps: Hiệu năng tải thực tế (Throughput, độ trễ và lượng tiêu thụ RAM) của reverse proxy viết bằng Go trong Gately so với Nginx thuần hoặc Nginx Proxy Manager khi xử lý tải cao.
Khả năng cấu hình FRP Server (frps) kết hợp với các FRP Client (frpc) từ xa hoạt động tự động ra sao trên giao diện web so với cách tạo file toml truyền thống.
Khi ISP chặn cổng 80/443 trên mạng gia đình, STUN traversal hay Cloudflare Tunnel trong Gately có thể tự động gánh traffic thay thế cho reverse proxy web mà không cần cấu hình thủ công hay không.
Có hỗ trợ đồng bộ hóa cấu hình (cluster / high availability) giữa nhiều node VPS và Homelab hay chỉ sao lưu dạng file JSON đơn lẻ.

## wangwanjie/gately (https://github.com/wangwanjie/gately)
Description: Open-source, auditable network gateway for homelabs, NAS and servers: DDNS, STUN traversal, port forwarding with SNI routing, reverse proxy and web server, ACME certificates, WAF, Tailscale, frp, Cloudflare Tunnel, Docker and web terminal in one binary. Runs on Docker, fnOS, OpenWrt, Linux, macOS and Windows.
Homepage: https://gately.cn
Language: Go; license: Apache-2.0; created 2026-10-15; last push 2026-11-09
Latest release: v0.6.5.2 (2026-11-08)
README (start):
Website  ·  Quick start  ·  Install guide  ·  Docs  ·  Download  ·  Changelog

  

  English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español | Français | Deutsch | Русский | Português (Brasil)

DNS and NAT traversal, reverse proxy and HTTPS certificates, WAF and intrusion prevention, single sign-on and file sharing: everything your home network and servers need at the edge, managed from one console. Run it on a NAS, a soft router or a cloud server and set it all up in your browser. Open source under Apache-2.0; your config and data stay on your own device, and nothing is collected or reported.

> **fnOS users:** Gately ships as a native fnOS app. It plugs into the **fnOS unified gateway**, so it opens from the fnOS desktop icon and works over the same address you use for fnOS, including your remote domain, with no extra port to open. Once enabled, **fnOS administrators can sign in directly with their fnOS session**, without a Gately password or two-step code. See [fnOS native app](https://gately.cn/en/docs/guide/install#fnos).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae5b60a4-9402-4a66-86a1-48e40038b4d0

## Quick Start

Three steps: start the container, open `http://:16680`, sign in with `admin` / `gately.cn`. Other platforms are below, and the [install guide](https://gately.cn/en/docs/guide/install) covers every option.

### Docker

Images are available for amd64, arm64, and arm/v7, published to GHCR and to Docker Hub as `vanjayak/gately` (same image and tags; use `vanjayak/gately:latest` if GHCR is hard to reach):

```bash
docker run -d --name gately --network host --cap-add NET_ADMIN \
  -v ./gately-data:/etc/gately \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  ghcr.io/wangwanjie/gately:latest
```

Open `http://:16680` and sign in with the default account `admin` and the default password `gately.cn`. Then change the password and enable two-factor authentication under Settings. See [deploy/docker-compose.yml](deploy/docker-compose.yml) for a complete Compose example.

If you forget the password or lose your authenticator, run `gately reset-password` or `gately reset-totp` on the server (`docker exec -it gately gately reset-password` for Docker); the change takes effect once you confirm. See [Reset password and two-factor authentication](https://gately.cn/en/docs/guide/install#reset).

Port forwarding, STUN, and web services listen on host ports, so `--network host` is recommended. If you do not need Docker management, drop the `docker.sock` mount. `--cap-add NET_ADMIN` lets Intrusion Prevention write bans to the host's nftables firewall; without it, bans still apply to Gately's own services.

Short on storage, for example on a router? [build.gately.cn](https://build.gately.cn) builds a binary, OpenWrt or fnOS package, or a multi-arch Docker image with only the modules and UI languages you pick.

Prefer another way to install? Pick one below.

Binary

Download the archive for your platform from [Releases](https://github.com/wangwanjie/gately/releases) (Linux amd64/arm64/arm/mips/mipsle/riscv64, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD), extract it, and run:

```bash
./gately -c /etc/gately
```

Flags: `-c` sets the config directory (the `GATELY_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable also works), `-listen` overrides the admin UI listen address, `-apply` applies `.json` files from a directory to the config directory on every start (`GATELY_APPLY_DIR`, handy for GitOps and Kubernetes; the account and token files cannot be overwritten), and `-version` prints the version. For unattended installs, set `GATELY_INITIAL_PASSWORD` to choose the initial admin password instead of the default `gately.cn`.

Start at boot: after extracting, run `sudo ./gately service install` (Windows: `.\gately.exe service install` in an administrator terminal). It registers a systemd unit on Linux, a launchd daemon on macOS (add `-user` for a login item without sudo) and a Windows service, starts Gately and brings it back after a crash; the config directory defaults to `/etc/gately`, `/usr/local/etc/gately` or `%ProgramData%\Gately` and `-c` and `-listen` override it. Keep the binary at its final location first, because the service points at that path. Use `gately service uninstall|start|stop|restart|status` to manage it afterwards; the config directory is kept when uninstalling.

Service templates: [systemd](deploy/systemd/gately.service) and [OpenWrt procd](deploy/openwrt/gately.init). To verify downloaded archives and images (cosign signatures, build provenance, SBOM), see [Verifying release artifacts](docs/en/VERIFY.md).

fnOS native app

Each Release ships offline `.fpk` packages for fnOS: `gately__fnos_x86.fpk` (Intel/AMD) and `gately__fnos_arm.fpk` (ARM). They are not in the official App Center, so install them manually: open **App Center → Manual install** (the button at the bottom-left), pick the file, and finish the wizard.

- **Works with the fnOS unified gateway**: click the Gately icon on the fnOS desktop and the admin UI opens through the fnOS unified gateway under `/app/gately/`, sharing the entry point you already use for fnOS. Both the LAN address and your remote fnOS domain work, with no need to open or forward port 16680. Access through the gateway is controlled by fnOS (only fnOS administrators can open it), so the safe entry and LAN-only settings apply only to direct access on port 16680.
- **Signs fnOS administrators in with their fnOS session**: turn on **Settings → Access control → Sign in with fnOS** and fnOS administrators who are signed in to fnOS enter Gately from the desktop icon without a password or two-step code; regular fnOS users still sign in. After you sign out, the login page offers a "Sign in as fnOS user <name>" button instead of signing you back in silently. The setting is off by default and only shown in the fnOS package.
- On the LAN the admin UI is also at `http://:16680`. The default account is `admin` and the default password is `gately.cn`.
- The app runs as `root`, so it can listen on 80/443, manage Docker through `docker.sock`, and open a real Web terminal. Install it only on a NAS you control.
- Config lives in the app's `var` directory and is kept on uninstall unless you choose "delete all" in the uninstall wizard. Upgrading is another manual install of the newer `.fpk`.
- The package also adds a `gately` command (`/usr/local/bin/gately`) for `gately ctl` and `gately mcp`.
- Port 16680 is shared with the Docker image. Stop the `gately` container before starting the native app.
- Verify the download as described in [Verifying release artifacts](docs/en/VERIFY.md); `.fpk` files are listed in `checksums.txt`.

OpenWrt

Each Release ships OpenWrt packages: `gately__openwrt_.ipk` for OpenWrt 24.10 and earlier (including iStoreOS), installed with `opkg install`, and `.apk` for OpenWrt 25.12 and later, installed with `apk add --allow-untrusted`. Packages cover amd64 / arm64 / arm / mipsle / mips / riscv64; pick one by `DISTRIB_ARCH` in `/etc/openwrt_release` (see the table in the [install guide](https://gately.cn/en/docs/guide/install#openwrt)).

- The service is enabled and started on install; the admin UI is at `http://:16680`, and the default account is `admin` with the password `gately.cn`.
- Config lives in `/etc/gately` and is kept across upgrades, uninstalls and firmware upgrades (sysupgrade). To upgrade, install the newer package; the online upgrade on the About page points you to the package manager instead.
- The binary is about 32 MB, so the packages suit x86 soft routers, ARM64 boxes and other devices with ample storage; the arm package needs ARMv7 with hardware floating point.
- An architecture-independent LuCI app, `luci-app-gately__openwrt_all.ipk` / `.apk`, adds **Services → Gately** to LuCI: service state, start / stop, start at boot, the admin port and a one-click link to the admin interface.

Monitoring

Create an API token with only the `metrics:read` permission and point Prometheus at `/api/metrics`. Metrics, alert examples and the Grafana dashboard are described in [Monitoring](docs/en/MONITORING.md).

API usage

Create a token on the "API Tokens" page of the admin console. You can create several, grant each read-only or read-write access per module, set an expiry, and the plaintext is shown only once, right after creation. Scripts can then call the admin API in bulk:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer gtl_xxxx" http://localhost:16680/api/ddns/tasks
```

Account, two-factor authentication, and token management, as well as the backup, restore, restart, and system settings endpoints, accept login sessions only. All endpoints, required permissions, and data schemas are listed on the "API Docs" page of the admin console. You can also export them to [docs/api/en](docs/api/en) (`openapi.json` and `API.md`) with `make api-docs`; the website https://gately.cn references them directly when published.

When upgrading from an older version, the previous global API token becomes a "legacy token" automatically (same value, full access to every module). Tighten its permissions or replace it with a new token on the API Tokens page.

Tailscale, NetBird, frp, cloudflared

These four modules manage the official external programs (automatic restart, logs aggregated in the UI). Gately does not bundle them. The "online install" card on each module page downloads the latest stable release or a specific version from upstream, verifies its SHA-256, installs it into `bin/` under the config directory and restarts the processes that use it; each program can have its own download proxy, and when it is empty the update proxy from Settings is used. The last 3 replaced versions are kept, so you can roll back with one click if a new version has problems, and a program you no longer need can be uninstalled. "Restore defaults" in the page header is separate from uninstalling: it stops the processes, resets the module settings and deletes the files Gately generated for it (frp config files, File Browser instance data, Tailscale and NetBird login state); the old settings can be restored from the config history. Tailscale only publishes ready-to-run packages for Linux; on other systems use the official installer and enter its path. Programs are located in this order: the path set in the module settings, `bin/` under the config directory, then `PATH`. You can also put the binary into the config directory yourself, for example `./gately-data/bin/frpc` in Docker deployments; Tailscale needs both `tailscale` and `tailscaled`. Tokens and keys in config files are stored with 0600 permissions, and the cloudflared token is passed via an environment variable so it never appears in the process list.

The File Browser module hosts [FileBrowser Quantum](https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser) (the original filebrowser is archived and no longer receives security fixes) with the same lookup order and the same online install, update and rollback as above, installed as `bin/filebrowser`. The admin password is passed via an environment variable and never written to the config file.

## Features

A quick tour of the admin UI. The full list of modules is at the end of this section.

### Everything at a glance

The overview shows CPU, memory, disk and traffic, network interfaces with their public IPv4 and IPv6, and the state of every module, so you can tell in seconds whether anything needs attention.

### Web services that can replace nginx

Reverse proxy, static files and redirects by domain, with HTTPS and HTTP/3. Each site gets its own WAF, IP rules and sign-in, and changes apply without dropping connections.

Per-site statistics — requests, errors, backend health, top client IPs and countries, minute by minute.

### Network topology

See how traffic flows from visitors through listeners and sites to backends, live. Pick a node for QPS, traffic and active IPs, filter by visitor IP, switch between seven layouts, and mask addresses before you share

## NginxProxyManager/nginx-proxy-manager (https://github.com/NginxProxyManager/nginx-proxy-manager)
Description: Docker container for managing Nginx proxy hosts with a simple, powerful interface
Homepage: https://nginxproxymanager.com
Language: JavaScript; license: MIT; created 2017-12-20; last push 2026-11-09
Latest release: v2.16.0 (2026-09-24)
README (start):
This project comes as a pre-built Docker image that enables you to easily forward to your websites
running at home or otherwise, including free SSL, without having to know too much about Nginx or Letsencrypt.

- [Quick Setup](#quick-setup)
- [Full Setup](https://nginxproxymanager.com/setup/)
- [Screenshots](https://nginxproxymanager.com/screenshots/)

## Project Goal

I created this project to fill a personal need to provide users with an easy way to accomplish reverse
proxying hosts with SSL termination, and it had to be so easy that a monkey could do it. This goal hasn't changed.
While there might be advanced options, they are optional, and the project should be as simple as possible
so that the barrier to entry here is low.

## Features

- Beautiful and Secure Admin Interface based on [Tabler](https://tabler.github.io/)
- Easily create forwarding domains, redirections, streams, and 404 hosts without knowing anything about Nginx
- Free SSL using Let's Encrypt or provide your own custom SSL certificates
- Access Lists and basic HTTP Authentication for your hosts
- Advanced Nginx configuration available for super users
- User management, permissions, and audit log

::: warning
`armv7` is no longer supported in version 2.14+. This is due to Nodejs dropping support for armhf. Please
use the `2.13.7` image tag if this applies to you.
:::

## Hosting your home network

I won't go into too much detail here, but here are the basics for someone new to this self-hosted world.

1. Your home router will have a Port Forwarding section somewhere. Log in and find it
2. Add port forwarding for ports 80 and 443 to the server hosting this project
3. Configure your domain name details to point to your home, either with a static ip or a service like
   - DuckDNS
   - [Amazon Route53](https://github.com/jc21/route53-ddns)
   - [Cloudflare](https://github.com/jc21/cloudflare-ddns)
4. Use the Nginx Proxy Manager as your gateway to forward to your other web-based services

## Quick Setup

1. [Install Docker](https://docs.docker.com/install/)
2. Create a docker-compose.yml file similar to this:

```yml
services:
  app:
    image: 'docker.io/jc21/nginx-proxy-manager:latest'
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '81:81'
      - '443:443'
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
      - ./letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt
```

This is the bare minimum configuration required. See the [documentation](https://nginxproxymanager.com/setup/) for more.

3. Bring up your stack by running

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

4. Log in to the Admin UI

When your docker container is running, connect to it on port `81` for the admin interface.
Sometimes this can take a little bit because of the entropy of keys.

[http://127.0.0.1:81](http://127.0.0.1:81)

## Contributing

All are welcome to create pull requests for this project, against the `develop` branch. Official releases are created from the `master` branch.

CI is used in this project. All PR's must pass before being considered. After passing,
docker builds for PR's are available on dockerhub for manual verifications.

Documentation within the `develop` branch is available for preview at
[https://develop.nginxproxymanager.com](https://develop.nginxproxymanager.com)

### Contributors

Special thanks to [all of our contributors](https://github.com/NginxProxyManager/nginx-proxy-manager/graphs/contributors).

## Getting Support

1. [Found a bug?](https://github.com/NginxProxyManager/nginx-proxy-manager/issues)
2. [Discussions](https://github.com/NginxProxyManager/nginx-proxy-manager/discussions)
3. [Reddit](https://reddit.com/r/nginxproxymanager)

## jpfranca-br/frps-setup (https://github.com/jpfranca-br/frps-setup)
Description: Automate the install and configuration of a clean Ubuntu server to run Fast Reverse Proxy - FRP https://github.com/fatedier/frp
Homepage: -
Language: Shell; license: none; created 2024-12-03; last push 2024-12-04
No releases
README (start):
# FRPS Server Configuration Script

This script is designed to configure and set up a [Fast Reverse Proxy Server - FRP](https://github.com/fatedier/frp) environment on a clean Ubuntu Linux server. It automates the process of configuring the server for domain-based reverse proxying and security using Let's Encrypt SSL certificates and FRP.

## Prerequisites

Before running this script, ensure you have:

1. A domain with DNS configured:
   - Create an **A record** in your DNS zone to point your server's name and the internal service(s) you want to access to a fixed public IP address.

   For the rest of this tutorial, let's assume:
   - Server: `server.foobar.com`
   - Internal service: `internal_service_name.foobar.com`

2. Access to a Linux server with su privileges.

---

## Steps for Configuration

### 1. Log in as root and create a new user for the FRPS service

Run the following commands to create a user (we will use `foobar` in this example):

```bash

ssh root@server.foobar.com
adduser foobar
usermod -aG sudo foobar
exit

```

### 2. Log in as the new user

Log in as the newly created user:

```bash

ssh foobar@server.foobar.com

```

### 3. Download and execute the setup script

Clone this repository and execute frps-setup.sh:

```bash
sudo apt install git -y && rm -rf frps-setup && git clone https://github.com/jpfranca-br/frps-setup.git && cd frps-setup && chmod +x frps-setup.sh && ./frps-setup.sh
```

### 4. Enter the required data

The script will prompt you to enter the following information:

- **Email Address**: Used for Certbot notifications.
- **Number of Domains**: The number of domains you want to configure.
- **Domain Names**: Enter each domain name one by one.
- **FRP Token**: Enter a secure token that will later be used by FRP clients to authenticate.
- **password**: Enter the password for the currently logged user

#### Example Inputs:

```text
Enter your email address (for Certbot notifications): foobar@foobar.com
Enter the number of domains: 2
Enter domain 1: server.foobar.com
Enter domain 2: internal_service_name.foobar.com
Enter the FRP token: abc-def-ghi-jkl
[sudo] password for foobar:
```

### 5. Wait for the script to complete

The script will perform all necessary configurations and display the following message upon successful completion:

```text
Setup complete for domains: server.foobar.com internal_service_name.foobar.com
```

That’s all you need to do on the server side!

---

## Client Configuration

For each client, configure the `frpc.toml` file as follows:

```toml
# frpc.toml
user = "foobar"

loginFailExit = false

serverAddr = "server.foobar.com" 
serverPort = 7000

auth.method = "token"
auth.token = "abc-def-ghi-jkl" 
# Use the token entered during server setup.

[[proxies]]
name = "internal_service_name" # Descriptive name for your service
type = "http"
localPort = 8096               # Internal port of your service
customDomains = ["internal_service_name.foobar.com"]
```

---

## What the Script Does

1. **System Updates and Dependencies**: Installs required packages such as `certbot`, `nginx`, and `apt-utils`.
2. **SSL Configuration**: Obtains Let's Encrypt certificates for the specified domains.
3. **Nginx Configuration**: Configures Nginx to proxy traffic securely to internal services.
4. **FRP Setup**:
   - Downloads and configures the FRP server.
   - Generates a secure `frps.toml` file.
   - Creates and enables the FRP service.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **Domain Resolution Issues**: Ensure your DNS A records are correctly configured to point to the server's IP.
- **Port Accessibility**: Ensure the necessary ports (22, 80, 443, 7000) are open on your server's firewall.
- **SSL Certificate Issues**: Check that your domains resolve correctly and Certbot can verify ownership.

---

## Credits

This script simplifies the process of setting up a secure FRP server environment. For more details about FRP, visit the [official FRP GitHub repository](https://github.com/fatedier/frp).

Installation
​
Docker
​

Image: ghcr.io/wangwanjie/gately, also published to Docker Hub as vanjayak/gately (the same image with the same tags), available for amd64, arm64 and arm/v7. If GHCR is hard to reach, replace the image name below with vanjayak/gately:latest; Docker registry mirrors work with it too.

bash
docker run -d --name gately --network host --cap-add NET_ADMIN \
  -v ./gately-data:/etc/gately \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  ghcr.io/wangwanjie/gately:latest
Docker Compose
​
yaml
services:
  gately:
    image: ghcr.io/wangwanjie/gately:latest
    container_name: gately
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Port forwarding, STUN traversal and web services all listen on host ports directly
    network_mode: host
    # Intrusion Prevention writes bans to the host firewall (remove if not needed)
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    volumes:
      # Config directory (plain JSON, safe to keep in git; ssl.json contains certificate private keys)
      - ./data:/etc/gately
      # Docker management (remove if not needed)
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    environment:
      - TZ=Asia/Shanghai

--cap-add NET_ADMIN and cap_add let Intrusion Prevention write bans to the host's nftables firewall. You can drop them; bans then still apply to Gately's own services.

The image ships with sh, bash and curl, so typical notification scripts run out of the box.

Binary
​
Get the archive for your platform from the download page: Linux (amd64 / arm64 / arm / mips / mipsle / riscv64), macOS, Windows or FreeBSD.
Extract it and run:
bash
./gately -c /etc/gately
Start at boot (gately service)
​

After extracting, move the binary to its final location (the service points at the current executable path), then run:

bash
sudo ./gately service install

On Windows, run .\gately.exe service install in an administrator terminal. Linux gets a systemd unit, macOS a launchd daemon (add -user to register a login item for the current user without sudo) and Windows a system service; Gately starts right away and is brought back after a crash. The config directory defaults to /etc/gately, /usr/local/etc/gately or %ProgramData%\Gately; -c sets another one, -listen sets the admin UI listen address and -no-start registers the service without starting it. Manage it afterwards with gately service uninstall|start|stop|restart|status; uninstalling keeps the config directory.

To customize the unit file, use the systemd template below instead.

systemd
​

The repository ships a complete service file, deploy/systemd/gately.service, which already grants the capability needed to listen on low ports:

bash
sudo install -m 0755 gately /usr/local/bin/gately
sudo install -m 0644 gately.service /etc/systemd/system/gately.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now gately
OpenWrt
​

Every release ships OpenWrt packages that contain the binary, the procd init script and a rule that keeps your config across firmware upgrades:

OpenWrt 24.10 and earlier (including iStoreOS and other 24.10-based firmware) use the .ipk, installed with opkg install;
OpenWrt 25.12 and later use the .apk, installed with apk add --allow-untrusted (the packages are unsigned, so --allow-untrusted is required).

Run grep DISTRIB_ARCH /etc/openwrt_release to find the device architecture, then pick the package from the OpenWrt group on the download page:

DISTRIB_ARCH	Package
x86_64	gately_<version>_openwrt_amd64
aarch64_*	gately_<version>_openwrt_arm64
arm_cortex-a*_* (ARMv7 with VFP / NEON)	gately_<version>_openwrt_arm
mipsel_*	gately_<version>_openwrt_mipsle
mips_*	gately_<version>_openwrt_mips
riscv64_*	gately_<version>_openwrt_riscv64
bash
cd /tmp
# OpenWrt 24.10 / iStoreOS (x86_64 shown)
opkg install ./gately_<version>_openwrt_amd64.ipk
# OpenWrt 25.12
apk add --allow-untrusted ./gately_<version>_openwrt_amd64.apk
The service is enabled at boot and started right after install; the admin UI is at http://<router address>:16680. Config lives in /etc/gately and is kept across firmware upgrades (sysupgrade);
Upgrade: download the newer package and run opkg install or apk add --allow-untrusted again; your config is kept. If you disabled the service at boot, it stays disabled after the upgrade;
Uninstall: opkg remove gately or apk del gately. The config directory is kept; run rm -rf /etc/gately to remove it as well;
The device architecture is checked before install. opkg aborts when the architecture does not match; the apk in OpenWrt 25.12 still installs the package but leaves the service stopped, so run apk del gately and install the right package;
The binary is about 32 MB and needs the same amount of free space (check with df -h /overlay), which suits x86 soft routers, ARM64 boxes and other devices with ample storage; routers with 16 MB / 32 MB of flash are too small;
The arm package needs ARMv7 with hardware floating point. ARMv5 / ARMv6 devices and FPU-less cores such as arm_cortex-a9 are not supported yet.

You can also deploy manually: download the Linux archive and use the procd init script deploy/openwrt/gately.init:

bash
cp gately /usr/bin/gately && chmod +x /usr/bin/gately
cp gately.init /etc/init.d/gately && chmod +x /etc/init.d/gately
/etc/init.d/gately enable && /etc/init.d/gately start
LuCI app
​

Each release also ships an architecture-independent LuCI app, luci-app-gately_<version>_openwrt_all.ipk / .apk. Install it after Gately:

bash
# OpenWrt 24.10 / iStoreOS
opkg install ./luci-app-gately_<version>_openwrt_all.ipk
# OpenWrt 25.12
apk add --allow-untrusted ./luci-app-gately_<version>_openwrt_all.apk

Then open Services → Gately in LuCI to:

see the service state, version, memory usage and whether it starts at boot;
start, stop and restart the service, and enable or disable start at boot;
open the Gately admin interface in one click, with the safe entrance from the global settings already in the link;
set the admin port. It is stored in /etc/config/gately and, when set, replaces the port of the listen address in the Gately global settings (a host part such as a loopback or LAN address is kept), which helps when the admin interface is unreachable because of a port conflict or a wrong port; leave it empty to follow the global settings.

Everything else is still configured in the Gately admin interface. The app follows the LuCI language and is translated into Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, Russian and Portuguese (Brazil). To uninstall, remove luci-app-gately first (opkg remove luci-app-gately or apk del luci-app-gately), then gately.

fnOS native app
​

Every release ships offline packages for fnOS: gately_<version>_fnos_x86.fpk (Intel / AMD) and gately_<version>_fnos_arm.fpk (ARM). They are not listed in the official App Center, so install them manually:

Get the .fpk for your device's architecture from the download page;
In fnOS, open "App Center → Manual install" (the button at the bottom-left), pick the file and finish the wizard;
Click the Gately icon on the fnOS desktop to open the admin UI.
Works with the fnOS unified gateway
​

The desktop icon opens the admin UI through the fnOS unified gateway at /app/gately/ on the address you use for fnOS, sharing the same entry point. Both the LAN address and your remote fnOS domain work, with no need to open or forward port 16680.

Access through the gateway is controlled by fnOS, and only fnOS administrators can open it. The secure entrance path and "LAN-only access" apply only to direct access on port 16680. On the LAN, http://<NAS address>:16680 still works.

Sign in with your fnOS administrator session
​

Turn on "Sign in with fnOS" under "Settings → Access control" and administrators who are signed in to fnOS enter Gately straight from the desktop icon, without a password or two-step code:

Only fnOS administrators are signed in, as the Gately administrator; regular fnOS users still enter a username and password;
It applies only to access through the unified gateway; direct access on port 16680 still requires a normal sign-in;
After you sign out, Gately does not sign you back in silently; the login page shows a "Sign in as fnOS user <name>" button instead;
The setting is off by default and only shown in the fnOS package.
Notes
​
The app runs as root, so it can listen on 80/443, manage Docker through docker.sock and open a real Web terminal. Install it only on a NAS you control.
Config lives in the app's var directory and is kept on uninstall unless you choose "delete all" in the uninstall wizard.
The package also adds a /usr/local/bin/gately command for gately ctl, gately mcp and gately reset-password.
Port 16680 is shared with the Docker image. Stop the gately container before starting the native app.
Initial sign-in
​

The admin UI listens on port 16680 by default. The default account is admin and the default password is gately.cn. For automated deployments, set the GATELY_INITIAL_PASSWORD environment variable to choose your own password instead of the default.

The default password is public; while it is still in use, the admin UI keeps showing a warning at the top asking you to change it. The first sign-in shows an onboarding guide that walks you through changing the password, enabling two-factor authentication or a Passkey, running the network self-check, importing from Lucky and setting up notifications.

Reset password and two-factor authentication
​

If you forget the administrator password or lose your two-factor authenticator (TOTP), reset it by running a command on the server where Gately runs. The command needs read and write access to the config directory, which is the same as having access to the server, so it cannot be used over the network:

gately reset-password: resets the administrator password to the default gately.cn; add -p <new password> to set a new password directly;
gately reset-totp: turns off two-factor authentication for the administrator; you can enable it again after signing in.

Before doing anything, the command shows the administrator username and the action it is about to take, and asks you to type yes to confirm so a slip of the keyboard does no harm; in scripts and other non-interactive environments, add -y to skip the confirmation. A running Gately applies the change within seconds without a restart; if Gately is not running, the change applies on the next start. A reset invalidates all signed-in sessions and clears login lockouts; the username, Passkeys, read-only accounts and other configuration stay unchanged.

Install method	Command
Docker	docker exec -it gately gately reset-password
systemd	sudo gately reset-password
OpenWrt / iStoreOS	gately reset-password
fnOS	sudo gately reset-password
Other	./gately reset-password -c <config dir>

Without -c, the command looks in GATELY_CONFIG_DIR, data in the current directory, /etc/gately and the fnOS package config directory /var/apps/gately/var/config, in that order, and prints the directory it uses. Resets are recorded in the system log and the audit log.

TCP / UDP hole punching and keep-alive, UPnP / NAT-PMP, automatic port opening in the host firewall, built-in forwarding; triggers webhooks and scripts when the public address changes.

FAQ
Does it need to connect to your servers?

No. Gately does not connect to any project servers and reports nothing; by default it anonymously checks GitHub for new releases and security advisories, which can be turned off.

Which devices can it run on?

Home NAS, soft routers, cloud hosts and servers of all kinds. Binaries are provided for Linux (amd64 / arm64 / arm / mips / mipsle / riscv64), macOS, Windows and FreeBSD, plus Docker images for amd64 / arm64 / arm/v7, a native app package for fnOS, and OpenWrt packages (.ipk / .apk).

Does it support fnOS?

Yes. Every release ships offline fnOS packages (.fpk) that you install manually from the App Center. Gately plugs into the fnOS unified gateway, so it opens from the desktop icon and also works over your remote fnOS domain. Turn on Sign in with fnOS under Settings → Access control and fnOS administrators who are signed in go straight in, without a password or two-step code.

Why is host networking recommended for port forwarding and STUN?

These modules listen directly on host ports. If you do not need Docker management, you can drop the docker.sock mount.
